1.meaning: He frowned — he knit his brow and his face contracted in displeasure or annoyance. The form describes a single completed act of scowling.

parts.en: he frowned (whole verb, 3rd-person masc. sing. past)

1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the basic Form I pattern faʿala (ʿa-ba-sa). The three root consonants ʿ-b-s carry the pattern vowels a-a-a; the final -a is the pattern's theme vowel sitting on the last root letter, not a subject suffix. The 3rd-person masculine singular ('he') is the unmarked default form — it is signalled precisely by the absence of any subject ending. Meaning: 'he frowned,' a completed action.
1.root: ع-ب-س (ʿ-b-s) — frowning, scowling, a face contracting in displeasure

2.meaning: And he turned away — he turned himself aside, averting his face and attention. The Form V (reflexive) pattern conveys a deliberate turning-of-oneself away.
2.grammar: Past-tense verb in Form V (tafaʿʿala), here tawallā. The ta- prefix makes the action reflexive ('turned himself'), and the doubled middle consonant (the shadda on the lām) is the structural hallmark of the Form V/II pattern. The weak final root letter appears as the long -ā ending. The 3rd-person masculine singular ('he') is unmarked, carrying no subject suffix; the preceding wa- means 'and.'
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — turning toward or away, facing, being adjacent

1.meaning: An — a subordinating particle with no single English word. Here it functions as 'because / on account of the fact that,' introducing the clause that gives the reason for the frowning (an underlying 'li-an,' 'for that...').
1.grammar: An invariable particle (it never changes its form). In this verse it introduces the cause of the action — best rendered 'because' — linking the preceding verbs to the clause 'the blind man came to him.' It carries no case ending of its own.

2.meaning: He came to him — someone arrived and presented himself before him. The verb is completed past action with an attached object 'him.'

parts.en: he came (whole verb, 3rd-person masc. sing. past)

2.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb, jāʾa ('he came'), built on a hollow root whose middle weak letter surfaces as the long -ā. The final -a on the last consonant is the perfect pattern's theme vowel, not a subject marker; the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he') is the unmarked default, shown by the absence of any subject suffix. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him,' so together: 'he came to him.'

3.meaning: The blind man — a person without sight. (The reference is to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Umm Maktūm, who came seeking instruction.) The word is the subject 'who came.'
3.grammar: A noun/adjective of the afʿal pattern (aʿmā, 'blind'), used here as a noun, 'the blind man,' with the definite article al-. Its final letter is a 'shortened alif' (the long -ā), one of the endings that never changes for case, so it looks the same whether subject or object; in this sentence it is the subject — the one who came.

1.meaning: But what / and what — the connective 'and/but' joined to the question-word 'what.' Together they open a rhetorical question: 'And what would make you realize...?'
1.grammar: Two invariable particles written together. Wa- is the connector 'and' (here best read 'but'); mā is the interrogative 'what,' standing as the subject of the following verb. Neither takes a case ending. The pairing launches a question that implies 'you cannot know.'

2.meaning: It makes you know / it informs you — it causes you to realize or be aware. In the rhetorical question 'what would make you know?,' it carries the sense 'what could possibly inform you?'
2.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb yudrī ('it makes [someone] know'), where the yu- prefix gives a 3rd-person masculine singular subject ('it') in the causative pattern, and the long -ī is the verb's weak ending. The attached -ka is the object 'you' (a single male, i.e. the Prophet): 'what makes you know?'

3.meaning: That perhaps he — laʿalla expresses hope or expectation ('perhaps, it may be that'), with 'he' attached. It frames the following clause as a hoped-for possibility: 'perhaps he...'
3.grammar: The particle laʿalla expresses hope or expectation and grammatically governs a noun or pronoun in the accusative. The attached pronoun -hu ('he/him') is its subject — written here with a long vowel (-hū) as the recitation requires. The phrase means 'perhaps he (might)...,' setting up the following verb.

4.meaning: He purifies himself — he cleanses his own soul, growing in inner purity and uprightness. The reflexive form means the purifying is done to oneself.
4.grammar: A present-tense reflexive verb, originally Form V yatazakkā ('he purifies himself'); in recitation the t of the prefix has merged into the z, giving the doubled yazzakkā. The ya- prefix marks the subject 'he,' and the long -ā is the verb's weak ending. Sense: 'he may purify himself.'
4.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — purity, growth, increase in goodness

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative between two possibilities ('purify himself' or 'be reminded'). Equivalent to English 'or.'
1.grammar: An invariable connecting particle meaning 'or.' It presents an alternative and takes no case ending of its own, linking the two hoped-for outcomes in the passage.

2.meaning: He takes heed / is reminded — he receives and reflects on a reminder or admonition, letting it sink in. The reflexive form conveys 'he brings the reminder home to himself.'

parts.en: plain present-tense ending ('he does / may do')

2.grammar: A present-tense reflexive verb, originally Form V yatadhakkaru ('he takes heed'); the t of the prefix has merged into the dh, giving the doubled yadhakkaru. The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u is the ordinary (indicative) present ending, stating the bare action: 'he takes heed / is reminded.'
2.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mindfulness, calling to mind

3.meaning: So that the reminder would benefit him — and as a result it (the reminder) would profit and be of use to him. The clause states the hoped-for outcome of his taking heed.
3.grammar: A present-tense Form I verb tanfaʿu ('it benefits'), with the ta- prefix giving a feminine 'it' subject (agreeing with the feminine 'reminder,' al-dhikrā). After the connector fa- ('so that'), the verb is in the subjunctive mood, shown by its final -a (instead of -u), expressing purpose or result: 'so that it would benefit him.' The attached -hu is the object 'him.'

4.meaning: The reminder; specifically the admonition, exhortation, and remembrance that comes through the revelation. In context it denotes the Qur'anic message that calls the heart back to Allah and benefits the one who heeds it.
4.grammar: A feminine noun built on the pattern fiʿlā, carrying the sense of an ongoing reminding. It begins with 'al-' (the), whose 'l' is here assimilated into the following emphatic 'dh' (so it sounds dh-dhikrā). The word ends in a fixed long 'ā' (written with alif maqsūra ٰى) that does not change for case; the small mark after it (here a pause sign) shows a stop. As the object of 'benefits him', it is functionally accusative even though the spelling stays the same.
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

1.meaning: As for…; a particle that opens a clause to single out and contrast one case from another ('As for X… , as for Y…'). It both emphasizes the topic it introduces and usually pairs with a following 'fa-' ('then/so') that begins the comment about that topic.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle of detail and contrast (no case ending, no root inflection). The doubled 'm' is intrinsic to the word. It sets up a topic and demands a 'fa-' clause in reply — here answered by 'fa-anta' in 80:6 ('As for the one who… , so you…'). The opening hamza carries 'a' (fatha).

2.meaning: Who / the one who; a relative-and-conditional pronoun used for persons ('he who', 'whoever'). Here it names the unspecified person about whom the statement is made: 'the one who…'.

parts.en: who / the one who (+ helping vowel -i)

2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun referring to a person; it never changes for case. Its base form is 'man'. The final 'i' here is not a case ending but a helping (linking) vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting when the next word ('istaghnā') begins with a silent connecting hamza — so it is read 'mani-staghnā'.

3.meaning: He considered himself self-sufficient and beyond need; he felt rich and independent, and so turned away — acting as though he had no need of guidance, of the message, or of Allah.

parts.en: Form X prefix: 'to deem/seek oneself to be…'
to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he…'), in the derived Form X (istafʿala), whose pattern adds the sense 'to regard oneself as' — here 'to regard oneself as free from need'. It opens with a connecting hamza ('i') that is dropped in continuous reading. It ends in the fixed long 'ā' (written ٰى) typical of this weak-final verb in the past tense; the mark after it shows a pause/recitation sign.
3.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

1.meaning: So you (singular); the word combines the connective 'so/then' with the pronoun 'you', addressing the Prophet directly. It opens the comment that answers the preceding 'As for…'.
1.grammar: Two pieces joined: the prefix 'fa-' ('so/then'), which here introduces the response to the 'ammā' ('as for') clause, plus the standalone subject pronoun 'anta' ('you', addressing one male). 'Anta' is a fixed pronoun with no case changes; its built-in ending '-a' is part of the word, not a grammatical case marker.

2.meaning: To him / for him; the preposition 'to/for' carrying the attached pronoun 'him'. Here it conveys directing one's attention toward that person ('to him you turned your attention').
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') with the third-person masculine singular pronoun 'him' attached to its end. The 'l' takes the vowel 'a' before the pronoun (la-), and the pronoun is pronounced 'hu' with a lengthened 'ū' (shown by the small wāw ٗ): 'lahū'. Whatever follows a preposition is grammatically genitive, and this pronoun is its object.

3.meaning: You turned toward (him) and gave (him) your full attention; you presented yourself to him and devoted yourself to engaging him, eagerly attending to him.

parts.en: to turn toward, attend to, devote attention

3.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you…'), addressing the Prophet. It is a Form V verb (tafaʿʿala, marked by the doubled middle consonant 'dd') carrying a reflexive/devoted sense — 'to set oneself to attend to'. The verb is weak-final, ending in the fixed long 'ā' (written ٰى); the original 't' of the Form V prefix has merged into this stem. (Originally tataṣaddā, with one 'ta' elided in recitation.) The mark after it is a pause sign.
3.root: ص-د-ي / ص-د-و (ṣ-d-y) — to turn toward, confront, attend to

1.meaning: But what / and what — the connective 'and/but' joined to the question-word 'what.' Together they open a rhetorical question: 'And what would make you realize...?'
1.grammar: Two invariable particles written together. Wa- is the connector 'and' (here best read 'but'); mā is the interrogative 'what,' standing as the subject of the following verb. Neither takes a case ending. The pairing launches a question that implies 'you cannot know.'

2.meaning: Upon you / against you; the preposition 'upon/on' with 'you' attached. Here it carries the sense of responsibility or blame resting on someone — 'it is not upon you (i.e. not your burden)'.
2.grammar: A preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on') whose ending shifts to 'ʿalay-' when a pronoun is attached, joined to the second-person masculine singular pronoun 'you' (-ka). The pronoun's '-a' ending is fixed for a single male addressee (a female would be '-ki'). Grammatically the attached pronoun is the genitive object of the preposition.

3.meaning: That… not; a fused particle meaning 'that he should not' or 'that… not'. It links a preceding word to a negated verb that follows, here introducing what one is 'not (responsible) for': 'that he is not purified'.
3.grammar: A contraction of two particles: 'an' ('that', which introduces and subjunctivizes a following verb) plus 'lā' ('not'). The 'n' of 'an' assimilates into the 'l' of 'lā', giving the doubled, run-together form 'allā'. It carries no case ending; it functions to introduce a negated clause ('that he not be purified').

4.meaning: He purifies himself — he cleanses his own soul, growing in inner purity and uprightness. The reflexive form means the purifying is done to oneself.
4.grammar: A present-tense reflexive verb, originally Form V yatazakkā ('he purifies himself'); in recitation the t of the prefix has merged into the z, giving the doubled yazzakkā. The ya- prefix marks the subject 'he,' and the long -ā is the verb's weak ending. Sense: 'he may purify himself.'
4.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — purity, growth, increase in goodness

1.meaning: But as for…; the connective 'and/but' joined to the contrasting particle 'as for'. It opens the opposite case to the one just described, turning attention to a new and contrasting subject.
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and/but') prefixed to the indeclinable particle of detail 'ammā' ('as for'). Like 'ammā' alone, it sets up a contrasting topic and calls for a following 'fa-' clause in answer ('But as for the one who… , then…'). None of these pieces take case endings; the doubled 'm' belongs to the word.

2.meaning: Who / the one who; a relative-and-conditional pronoun used for persons ('he who', 'whoever'). It names the contrasting unspecified person: 'the one who came to you…'.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun referring to a person; it never changes for case. Here it appears in its base form 'man' with a silent (sukūn) ending, because the next word ('jāa-ka') begins with a pronounced consonant, so no helping vowel is needed (contrast 'mani' in 80:5).

3.meaning: He came to you; someone approached and presented himself before you — here, the eager seeker who came to the Prophet desiring guidance.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he came'), with the object pronoun 'you' (-ka, addressing one male) attached. The verb's built-in '-a' ending is its standard past-tense form for 'he'. This is a doubly-weak (hollow + hamzated) root: its middle radical is the weak 'y' (ي), which surfaces as the long 'ā' (the hollow feature, جَا-), while its third radical is a separate hamza (ء, the final ءَ) — two distinct features, not one. The attached '-ka' is the direct object — 'he came (to) you'.

4.meaning: He strives, exerts effort, hastens eagerly toward something. The sense combines running/hurrying with earnest striving — here, the blind man who came eagerly seeking to learn.

parts.en: he (3rd-person masc. singular prefix on a present-tense verb)

4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he strives / is striving'). The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer. The verb ends in a weak final letter (alif maqsura, the -ā sound); because it is a defective root ending in a weak letter, the indicative mood is shown by that final -ā remaining in place rather than by a visible -u vowel.
4.root: س-ع-ي (s-ʿ-y) — to strive, exert effort, hasten/run

1.meaning: 'And he…' — a connecting word joining a new descriptive clause, with 'he' as its subject. Here it introduces a circumstantial clause: 'while he…', describing the state of the person.
1.grammar: A prefixed conjunction wa- ('and/while') attached to the standalone pronoun huwa ('he'). Functioning here as a circumstantial 'while he…', it sets up a description of the subject's accompanying state. The pronoun huwa is a fixed, indeclinable word; its final -a vowel never changes for case.

2.meaning: He fears, stands in awe, holds reverent dread. More than fright: a respectful, Allah-conscious awe that produces care and humility — here, the awe of Allah.

parts.en: he (3rd-person masc. singular prefix on a present-tense verb)
fear / stand in reverent awe (verb stem)

2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he fears / is in awe'). The ya- prefix marks 'he' as the doer. Being a defective root ending in a weak letter, its indicative mood is carried by the final weak -ā (alif maqsura) standing in place, rather than by an audible -u case-style ending.
2.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear, to be in reverent awe

1.meaning: So you (singular); the word combines the connective 'so/then' with the pronoun 'you', addressing the Prophet directly. It opens the comment that answers the preceding 'As for…'.
1.grammar: Two pieces joined: the prefix 'fa-' ('so/then'), which here introduces the response to the 'ammā' ('as for') clause, plus the standalone subject pronoun 'anta' ('you', addressing one male). 'Anta' is a fixed pronoun with no case changes; its built-in ending '-a' is part of the word, not a grammatical case marker.

2.meaning: 'From him' / 'away from him' / 'about him' — indicating turning or being diverted away from someone. Here: you turned away from / were inattentive to him.
2.grammar: The preposition ʿan ('away from / concerning') with the attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The pronoun is the object of the preposition. The -hu form takes a light u-vowel here (rather than -hi) because the preceding letter carries a sukun (no vowel), so the pronoun is voiced as -hu.

3.meaning: He becomes distracted, preoccupied, lets himself be diverted — turning his attention to something else and away from what matters. Here: you allowed yourself to be diverted (to him / by other concerns).

parts.en: you (2nd-person masc. singular subject prefix), fused with the Form V pattern's own ta-
be distracted / divert oneself / be preoccupied (Form V verb stem, with doubled middle root letter)

3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 2nd-person masculine singular ('you let yourself be distracted'). The verb is Form V (tafaʿʿala pattern), whose defining feature is a ta- built into the verb pattern itself plus a doubled middle root letter (shadda) giving a reflexive/intensive sense — 'to busy/divert oneself.' The full imperfect would be tatalahhā, with two consecutive ta- sounds: the first the 2ms subject-marker, the second the Form V pattern's ta-. Here one of the identical ta- syllables is dropped (haplology), so the single surviving تَـ does double duty — it is the Form V morphological ta-, not merely an ordinary person-prefix. As a defective verb ending in a weak letter, the mood is shown by the final -ā (alif maqsura) holding its place rather than by a visible short vowel.

1.meaning: A sharp word of rebuke and restraint: 'No! Not at all! Stop that!' It rejects the preceding attitude and calls the listener back. It is not merely 'no' to a question but a corrective 'by no means — desist.'

parts.en: no indeed! / by no means! / stop! (particle of rebuke and deterrence)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle of rebuttal and restraint. It takes no endings and changes form for nothing; its function is to negate and rebuke what came before and to deter the listener. The long final -ā is simply part of the fixed word.

2.meaning: 'Indeed it…' — an emphasis word stressing the truth of what follows, with 'it' (feminine) as the subject. The 'it' refers back to the revelation/this Qur'an. Conveys: 'Truly, it is…'

parts.en: indeed / truly (particle of emphasis and assertion)

2.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed') with the attached pronoun -hā ('it', feminine) as its subject. Inna powerfully affirms the statement that follows and grammatically governs its subject in the accusative; here that subject is the attached -hā. The feminine -hā points back to a feminine noun (the reminder/revelation).

3.meaning: A reminder, an admonition — something that brings truth back to mind and stirs heedfulness. A means of recollection that awakens the heart to what it should not forget.

parts.en: a reminder / admonition / means of remembrance
indefinite nominative ending ('a …', as the subject/predicate)

3.grammar: A feminine verbal noun built on the ta- pattern meaning 'a means of reminding.' The final ending is -un (tanwīn / nunation), which marks it as indefinite ('a reminder') and in the nominative case — fitting because it serves as the predicate of inna ('it is a reminder'). The -un ending is the nominative form.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to remind

1.meaning: 'So whoever…' — links to what came before ('so/therefore') and introduces a conditional 'whoever / the one who.' It sets up: whoever does X, the result is Y.

parts.en: so / then / therefore (connecting particle showing result)
whoever / the one who (conditional relative pronoun for people)

1.grammar: The prefix fa- ('so, then') drawing a consequence, joined to man ('whoever'), a conditional pronoun used for persons. Man here sets up a condition ('whoever wills…') whose answer follows. Man is indeclinable — a fixed form that takes no case endings.

2.meaning: He willed, wished, desired — to want or choose something. Here, in a conditional sense: 'whoever wills / wishes' (to be reminded).

parts.en: he willed / wished / desired (past-tense verb, 3rd-person masc. singular)

2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he willed / wished.' The 3ms perfect carries no separate suffix (a zero ending) — the final -a is simply the vowel on the third root letter (the hamza ء, the last radical of ش-ي-أ), not a detachable grammatical ending. The long -ā within the stem comes from the weak middle letter of the root. Though past in form, after the conditional man it carries the sense 'whoever wills.'
2.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to desire

3.meaning: He remembered it / called it to mind / took heed of it. To bring something back into one's awareness and act mindfully of it — here, to heed the reminder.

parts.en: he remembered / called to mind / took heed (past-tense verb)
it / him (attached 3rd-person masc. singular object pronoun)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he remembered'), built on the simple verb pattern with each root letter voweled -a-a-a (dhakara). The attached -hu ('it') is the direct object — the thing remembered. The -hu (rather than -hi) is voiced because the verb ends in the vowel -a before it.
3.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to take heed

1.meaning: 'In / on / within' — a preposition placing something inside or upon something else. Here: 'on / in [honoured] pages.'
1.grammar: A preposition meaning 'in / within / on.' It governs the noun after it (putting that noun in the genitive), expressing location or containment. Fī is a fixed particle with a long -ī vowel; it takes no endings itself and does not change form.

2.meaning: Pages, sheets, or leaves of writing — the written scrolls or folios on which a text is recorded. Here it refers to the honoured scriptural pages on which the Qur'an is inscribed.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun, indefinite ('some pages'). The final '-in' (the doubled bottom marks, called tanwīn) is the genitive case with indefinite '-n': it is genitive because it follows the preposition 'fī' ('in/on') from the previous phrase — 'on pages'. The plural form (singular ṣaḥīfa) means more than two.
2.root: ص-ح-ف (ṣ-ḥ-f) — to write on a flat surface; a leaf/page of writing

3.meaning: Honoured, held in high esteem, treated with dignity and nobility — made the object of honour and reverence by Allah.
3.grammar: A passive participle ('one that has been honoured') in the feminine, describing the 'pages' (ṣuḥuf). The 'mu-' prefix plus the doubled middle letter marks the intensive Form II pattern (mukarram-), conveying thorough, emphatic honouring. The feminine '-at' agrees with the feminine plural 'pages'. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is indefinite genitive, matching 'pages' which it describes.

1.meaning: Raised high, elevated, exalted in rank and status — lifted up in honour and made lofty.
1.grammar: A passive participle (ism al-mafʿūl, 'one that has been raised') in the feminine, describing the 'pages'. It is the Form I passive participle, which follows the fixed mafʿūl template (مَفْعُول): the 'ma-' and the long 'ū' are not separable affixes but part of this whole pattern, here filled by the root r-f-ʿ to give marfūʿ ('made raised/elevated'). The feminine '-at' agrees with 'pages'. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is indefinite genitive, matching the noun it qualifies.

2.meaning: Purified, cleansed, made spotless — kept free of all impurity, error, and defilement so that only the pure may touch it.
2.grammar: A passive participle ('one that has been purified') in the feminine, describing the 'pages'. The 'mu-' prefix with the doubled middle letter is the intensive Form II pattern (muṭahhar-), stressing complete, thorough purification. The feminine '-at' agrees with 'pages'. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is indefinite genitive, matching the noun described.
2.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanliness, freedom from defilement

1.meaning: In or by the hands of — denoting agency and careful handling: the pages are carried and transcribed 'at the hands of' those entrusted with them.
1.grammar: Preposition 'bi-' ('with/by') attached to 'aydī' ('hands'), the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' ('hand'). The long '-ī' is the inherent characteristic vowel of this broken-plural form, not a case ending. The noun is in the genitive case here for two reasons: it follows the preposition 'bi-', and it is the first term of a construct (iḍāfa, 'the hands OF...') leading into the next word 'safara' ('scribes') — 'by the hands of scribes'. The genitive is not separately visible because the broken plural's own '-ī' carries the form.

2.meaning: Scribes, writers, recorders — those who transcribe and travel with the message. Here it refers to noble angel-scribes entrusted with the revelation.
2.grammar: A plural noun on the broken-plural pattern faʿalah (فَعَلَة, with feminine tāʾ; singular sāfir, 'a scribe / one who travels'), indefinite. It is in the genitive case because it completes the construct phrase begun by 'aydī' — 'the hands OF scribes'. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending.
2.root: س-ف-ر (s-f-r) — to write/record; also to travel, to make clear

1.meaning: Noble, honourable, generous, of high and excellent character — exalted in worth and virtue.
1.grammar: An adjective in the plural (singular karīm, 'noble'), indefinite, describing the 'scribes' (safara). It is genitive to agree with 'scribes', which is itself genitive. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending, matching the noun it qualifies.

2.meaning: Dutiful, righteous, devoutly obedient — those who are faithful in fulfilling their obligations and abundant in piety and good conduct.
2.grammar: An adjective/noun in the plural (singular bārr, 'dutiful/pious'), indefinite, further describing the 'scribes'. It is genitive to agree with 'scribes'. The final '-in' (tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending. Paired with 'kirām' it forms the praise 'noble and dutiful'.

1.meaning: Literally 'he was killed/slain', used here as an imprecation: 'may he be destroyed / cursed / condemned' — a forceful expression of reproach against ungrateful humankind.
1.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb in the passive voice, 3rd person masculine singular ('he was killed'). The 3ms perfect takes no overt person suffix (a zero ending); the subject 'he' is implicit in the bare verb form. The internal vowel pattern qu-ti-la marks the passive — short vowels sit on the three root letters q-t-l, and the final fatḥa (-a) is simply the vowel on the last radical (lām), part of that pattern, not a person marker. Idiomatically the verb functions as a curse — 'may he be destroyed' — expressing condemnation.
1.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay; (idiomatically) to curse/destroy

2.meaning: The human being, mankind, the human creature — humanity considered as a species, here charged with ingratitude toward its Creator.
2.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the', and 'insān' is 'human being'. The final '-u' marks the nominative case, showing that 'the human' is the grammatical subject — here the one upon whom the curse falls ('the human is cursed / how cursed is the human'). With the article it denotes the human species in general.

3.meaning: An exclamatory 'how...!' — here it introduces astonishment and rebuke at the depth of humankind's ingratitude ('how ungrateful he is!'). It is not the ordinary question-word 'what', but a particle expressing wonder.
3.grammar: An exclamatory particle (mā al-taʿajjubiyya), used to express amazement or reproach: 'How greatly...!' It takes no case ending of its own and governs the verb that follows ('akfarahu'). It is distinct from interrogative 'mā' ('what?') and from negating 'mā' ('not'); context here marks it as the exclamation of wonder.

4.meaning: 'How ungrateful / disbelieving he is!' — an exclamation marvelling at the extreme ingratitude of the human being toward Allah, who denies and rejects His evident favours.

parts.en: to be ungrateful / to disbelieve, reject (Form IV perfect)

4.grammar: A verb of exclamation/wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub) built on the Form IV perfect pattern afʿala (أَفْعَلَ), here from the root k-f-r to give 'akfara'. The final fatḥa (-a) is the regular vowel on the last root letter of this 3ms perfect pattern — the same phenomenon as in qutila — not a special ending added by the taʿajjub construction. With the preceding 'mā', the sense is fixed as 'How ungrateful he is!' The attached '-hu' ('him') is the grammatical object of the exclamatory construction but refers to the human being himself, whose ingratitude is being marvelled at.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; hence ingratitude, denial, disbelief

1.meaning: A preposition meaning 'from' — it marks origin, source, or starting point: out of, from, made of. Here it asks about the material origin of a human being.
1.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (it never changes form). It governs the word after it, putting that word into the genitive case. Here it links to 'ayyi shay'in' to ask 'OUT OF what thing…?'

2.meaning: An interrogative word meaning 'which?' or 'what (kind of)?' Used to ask which one out of a set; here it questions which sort of substance man was made from.
2.grammar: An interrogative noun meaning 'which?'. The final -i ending is genitive because it follows the preposition 'min' ('from'). It is also in a possessive link with the next word: 'which OF a thing', i.e. 'what kind of thing'.

3.meaning: 'Thing' — an entity, something, any item or substance whatsoever. The broadest word for 'a thing' in Arabic; here it means the material or substance man was created from.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -in ending (called tanwīn, the doubled vowel that signals 'a/an') marks it as indefinite ('a thing'), and the -i sound within it is genitive, because it is governed by 'min' and stands in a possessive link after 'ayyi'. Literally: 'from which of a thing'.

4.meaning: 'He created him' — Allah brought him (the human being) into existence from nothing, fashioning and originating him.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'He created' — the subject is Allah. The final -a on the verb stem is the normal past-tense ending for 'he (did)'. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him', the one created.

1.meaning: A preposition meaning 'from' — it marks origin, source, or starting point: out of, from, made of. Here it asks about the material origin of a human being.
1.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (it never changes form). It governs the word after it, putting that word into the genitive case. Here it links to 'ayyi shay'in' to ask 'OUT OF what thing…?'

2.meaning: 'A sperm-drop' — a single drop of fluid (semen); the tiny amount of fluid from which a human is conceived.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -a is its feminine ending). The -in ending (tanwīn, the doubled vowel meaning 'a/an') marks it indefinite. It is in the genitive case because it is a badal (an appositive substitute) standing in for the earlier genitive noun 'shay'in' ('a thing') and matching its case — 'from a thing, [namely] from a sperm-drop'. The doubled n at the start (nn-) is assimilation of the n of the preceding 'min'.
2.root: ن-ط-ف (n-ṭ-f) — to drip, trickle; a drop of fluid

3.meaning: 'He created him' — Allah brought him (the human being) into existence from nothing, fashioning and originating him.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'He created' — the subject is Allah. The final -a on the verb stem is the normal past-tense ending for 'he (did)'. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him', the one created.

4.meaning: 'Then He proportioned him' — Allah determined, measured out, and gave him due proportions; He decreed his make-up, stages, and destiny in exact measure.
4.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'then / and so', showing the next step in sequence. The verb is past-tense, 3rd-person masculine singular — 'He proportioned' (subject: Allah) — with its -a being the past-tense 'he (did)' ending. This is the intensive (form II) verb, so it carries the sense of careful, deliberate measuring. The attached -hu is 'him'.
4.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — to measure, decree, determine power/extent

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then / thereafter'. Unlike 'fa-' (immediate sequence), 'thumma' marks a later stage with an interval or a step up in importance.
1.grammar: An indeclinable connecting particle (it never changes form). It joins what follows to what came before, signalling a sequence in time or rank with some delay — 'and then, after that'.

2.meaning: 'The way / the path' — a road or course to travel. In context it means the path of life and conduct, or the passage by which the infant comes into the world.
2.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its l assimilates into the following s, so it sounds 'as-sabīl'). The final -a ending is accusative, marking it as the direct object that comes before its verb — 'the way' is the thing made easy in 'yassarahu'.

3.meaning: 'He made it easy' — Allah smoothed and facilitated it, removing difficulty; He made the path/way easy to travel.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular — 'He made easy' (subject: Allah) — its -a being the past-tense 'he (did)' ending. It is the intensive (form II) verb, stressing a thorough easing. The attached -hu ('it / him') refers back to 'the way' (al-sabīl), which is named first for emphasis.
3.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy; ease, facility

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then / thereafter'. Unlike 'fa-' (immediate sequence), 'thumma' marks a later stage with an interval or a step up in importance.
1.grammar: An indeclinable connecting particle (it never changes form). It joins what follows to what came before, signalling a sequence in time or rank with some delay — 'and then, after that'.

2.meaning: 'He caused him to die' — Allah made him die; He brought about his death and took his life.

parts.en: he caused to die / put to death

2.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular — 'He caused to die' (subject: Allah) — its final -a being the past-tense 'he (did)' ending. The 'a-' built into the stem is causative (form IV): not 'he died' but 'he MADE (someone) die'. The attached -hu is 'him', the one made to die.

3.meaning: 'And He gave him a grave' — Allah caused him to be buried, providing him a grave; He honoured the dead body by having it placed in the earth rather than left exposed.

parts.en: he provided a grave / caused to be buried

3.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'then / and so', showing the next step. The verb is past-tense, 3rd-person masculine singular — 'He provided a grave' (subject: Allah) — its -a being the past-tense 'he (did)' ending. The 'a-' in the stem is causative (form IV): He CAUSED him to have a grave. The attached -hu is 'him'.

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then / thereafter'. Unlike 'fa-' (immediate sequence), 'thumma' marks a later stage with an interval or a step up in importance.
1.grammar: An indeclinable connecting particle (it never changes form). It joins what follows to what came before, signalling a sequence in time or rank with some delay — 'and then, after that'.

2.meaning: An adverb/conjunction meaning 'when' — referring to a future moment whose arrival is taken as certain: 'when (the time comes that)…'. It sets up the condition for what follows ('when He wills, He raises him').
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of time (it never changes form). It introduces a clause about the future treated as sure to happen, and looks ahead to a main response clause — 'WHEN He wills…, [then] He will resurrect him'.

3.meaning: He willed, wished, desired — to want or choose something. Here, in a conditional sense: 'whoever wills / wishes' (to be reminded).

parts.en: he willed / wished / desired (past-tense verb, 3rd-person masc. singular)

3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine singular: 'he willed / wished.' The 3ms perfect carries no separate suffix (a zero ending) — the final -a is simply the vowel on the third root letter (the hamza ء, the last radical of ش-ي-أ), not a detachable grammatical ending. The long -ā within the stem comes from the weak middle letter of the root. Though past in form, after the conditional man it carries the sense 'whoever wills.'
3.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to desire

4.meaning: He brought (him) back to life; He raised (him) up. The verb describes spreading out and reviving — Allah's act of resurrecting the dead, here with 'him' as the one resurrected.

parts.en: he brought to life / raised up

4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 'he' as the doer (Allah). Though past in form, it conveys the certainty of an act Allah does. The attached -hu is the direct object 'him' — the one being resurrected. There is no case ending on the verb itself; the final -a of 'anshara' is simply the verb's built-in vowel.
4.root: ن-ش-ر (n-sh-r) — to spread out, unfold, and (of the dead) to revive and raise

1.meaning: A sharp word of rebuke and restraint: 'No! Not at all! Stop that!' It rejects the preceding attitude and calls the listener back. It is not merely 'no' to a question but a corrective 'by no means — desist.'

parts.en: no indeed! / by no means! / stop! (particle of rebuke and deterrence)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle of rebuttal and restraint. It takes no endings and changes form for nothing; its function is to negate and rebuke what came before and to deter the listener. The long final -ā is simply part of the fixed word.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'not yet' — it negates a past action while implying that it still has not happened up to now (and may yet be expected). Here: 'he has not yet fulfilled.' It carries a sense of 'so far, not.'
2.grammar: A negating particle that governs the present-tense verb after it but gives it a completed, past meaning ('has not yet done'). It is built (indeclinable) and has no case ending; the final -ā is part of the fixed word. It implies the action remains awaited.

3.meaning: He carried out, completed, or fulfilled. The verb means to decree and bring something fully to completion. In context: man 'has not yet fulfilled' what Allah commanded of him.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, 'he' as the doer, here negated by the preceding 'lammā' to mean 'he has not yet fulfilled.' This is a defective verb (its root ends in a weak letter, ي). The negating particle puts it in the jussive ('cut-short') mood, and the mark of the jussive here is the DELETION of that final weak letter ي altogether, leaving the ض with a silent (vowelless) ending. The short -i heard in 'yaqḍi' is not a leftover of the dropped ī and not a case ending; it is a helping-vowel added onto the ض only to avoid an awkward consonant cluster before the next word.
3.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, complete, carry out fully

4.meaning: An exclamatory 'how...!' — here it introduces astonishment and rebuke at the depth of humankind's ingratitude ('how ungrateful he is!'). It is not the ordinary question-word 'what', but a particle expressing wonder.
4.grammar: An exclamatory particle (mā al-taʿajjubiyya), used to express amazement or reproach: 'How greatly...!' It takes no case ending of its own and governs the verb that follows ('akfarahu'). It is distinct from interrogative 'mā' ('what?') and from negating 'mā' ('not'); context here marks it as the exclamation of wonder.

5.meaning: He ordered (him); He commanded (him). The act of issuing a command. Here Allah is the one who commanded, and 'him' (man) is the one commanded.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, 'he' as the doer (Allah). The attached -hu is the direct object 'him' — the one commanded. The verb carries no case ending; the -a of 'amara' is the verb's own vowel.

1.meaning: Then let (him) look / consider / reflect. A command-by-implication: 'so let the person look closely.' Joining 'then/so' with a softly-issued order to observe and ponder.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb 'he looks,' turned into a third-person command ('let him look') by the prefixed 'li-' of command (here pronounced just 'l-' after 'fa-'). That command-prefix puts the verb in the jussive ('cut-short') mood, whose ending would be a vowelless -r; the final -i seen here is not a case ending but an extra helping-vowel added only to ease pronunciation before the next word ('ilā'). The leading 'fa-' means 'then/so.'
1.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, observe, consider, reflect

2.meaning: The human being, mankind, the human creature — humanity considered as a species, here charged with ingratitude toward its Creator.
2.grammar: A definite noun: 'al-' is 'the', and 'insān' is 'human being'. The final '-u' marks the nominative case, showing that 'the human' is the grammatical subject — here the one upon whom the curse falls ('the human is cursed / how cursed is the human'). With the article it denotes the human species in general.

3.meaning: To, toward, at — a preposition marking the goal or endpoint of an action. With 'look,' it gives 'look at / toward.' It points attention to something.
3.grammar: A preposition; it puts the following noun into the genitive case (the 'of/to' case). It is itself a fixed, built word with no case ending; the final -ā is part of the word. It directs the verb's action toward its object.

4.meaning: His food — that which is eaten; nourishment. The thing a person consumes, here attached to 'his.'
4.grammar: A noun, 'food,' with the possessive ending -hi ('his') attached. The noun sits in the genitive case because the preposition 'ilā' ('to/toward') comes before it; that genitive is why the pronoun appears as -hi (with an 'i' vowel) rather than -hu. So: 'toward HIS food.'

1.meaning: That We… — a particle of emphasis ('indeed/that') fused with 'We.' It introduces and stresses the statement that follows: '[consider] that We…' It both opens a content-clause and underlines its truth.
1.grammar: The emphatic particle 'anna' ('that / indeed') with the attached pronoun -nā ('we') as its subject. 'Anna' introduces a 'that…'-clause and gives it emphasis; it places its subject in the accusative, which is why the doer here is the attached -nā. The particle itself is fixed and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: We poured down. The act of pouring out a liquid abundantly — here, Allah pouring down the rain-water.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The attached -nā is the subject ending 'we,' marking the doer — 'we poured.' This is the royal 'We' of Allah. The -nā ending fixes the verb in this person, and the verb takes no separate case ending.
2.root: ص-ب-ب (ṣ-b-b) — to pour, pour out, pour down

3.meaning: The water — here specifically the rain-water that Allah pours down.
3.grammar: The definite noun 'the water.' The final -a ending is the accusative case: it marks this word as the direct object of 'we poured' — the thing that was poured. So it answers 'poured WHAT? — the water.' The 'al-' is 'the.'

4.meaning: An abundant pouring; a pouring down in plenty. It restates the verb 'poured' as a noun to intensify it — 'poured a real pouring,' i.e. copiously.
4.grammar: A verbal noun ('a pouring') used to reinforce its own verb. The -an ending is the accusative with 'nunation' (the indefinite 'n'-sound), here marking it as an emphasizing object that doubles the verb's force — 'we poured it down with a mighty pouring,' i.e. abundantly. The indefinite -an shows it is not 'the' pouring but 'a' pouring.
4.root: ص-ب-ب (ṣ-b-b) — to pour, pour out, pour down

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then / thereafter'. Unlike 'fa-' (immediate sequence), 'thumma' marks a later stage with an interval or a step up in importance.
1.grammar: An indeclinable connecting particle (it never changes form). It joins what follows to what came before, signalling a sequence in time or rank with some delay — 'and then, after that'.

2.meaning: We split open; We cleaved apart. Forcefully breaking something open — here Allah splitting open the earth so that growth may emerge.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The attached -nā is the subject ending 'we,' marking the doer — 'we split.' This is the royal 'We' of Allah. The -nā fixes the verb in this person, and the verb takes no separate case ending.
2.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave, tear open

3.meaning: The earth, the ground — the land/soil that is split open so that vegetation can sprout from it.
3.grammar: A definite noun, 'the earth.' The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative ending, marking it as the direct object of the verb — it is the thing that is being split open. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the' earth).

4.meaning: A splitting, a cleaving open — here an emphatic verbal noun reinforcing the verb, conveying that the earth is split open thoroughly and decisively.
4.grammar: A verbal noun (the action 'splitting') in the accusative, shown by the final -an (tanwīn fatḥ, 'an indefinite'). It functions as an 'absolute object': repeating the verb's own meaning as a noun to intensify it — 'We split it open with a real splitting,' i.e. thoroughly. The -an also signals it is indefinite ('a').
4.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave, tear open

1.meaning: Then We caused (plants) to grow — Allah making vegetation sprout and spring up from the soil.
1.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb in the causative form, meaning 'to make grow' rather than simply 'to grow.' The attached -nā ending is the subject 'we' (the royal 'We' of Allah). The fa- prefix means 'then/so,' linking this act to the previous one in sequence.
1.root: ن-ب-ت (n-b-t) — to grow, sprout, bring forth vegetation

2.meaning: In it, therein — within the earth that was split open.
2.grammar: A preposition 'in' with an attached pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine), referring back to the earth (a feminine noun). Together: 'in it / therein.' Pronouns after a preposition take this attached form; there is no case ending to explain.

3.meaning: Grain, seed-corn — edible cereal grains such as wheat and barley.
3.grammar: A noun in the accusative, marked by the final -an (tanwīn fatḥ), because it is the direct object of 'We caused to grow' — grain is the thing made to grow. The -an also marks it as indefinite ('grain' in general, not 'the grain').

1.meaning: And grapes — the grapevine and its fruit, listed among the things made to grow.
1.grammar: 'And grapes.' The wa- prefix means 'and,' joining it to the earlier 'grain.' The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative ending, since this too is a direct object of 'We caused to grow,' and marks it as indefinite.

2.meaning: And green fodder — fresh, succulent herbage/clover cut for grazing animals (it regrows after cutting).
2.grammar: 'And green fodder.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative ending — another item in the list of things made to grow — and marks it as indefinite. The name itself comes from a root meaning 'to cut,' since this plant is repeatedly cut for fodder.
2.root: ق-ض-ب (q-ḍ-b) — to cut, lop off (hence cut greens/fodder)

1.meaning: And olives — the olive tree and its fruit.
1.grammar: 'And olives.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative ending, since it continues the list of things Allah made to grow, and marks it as indefinite.

2.meaning: And date-palms — palm trees, a staple food source.
2.grammar: 'And date-palms.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The word is a collective noun (palm trees as a group). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) is the accusative ending — still part of the list of things made to grow — and marks it as indefinite.

1.meaning: And gardens, enclosed orchards — walled plots planted densely with trees.
1.grammar: 'And gardens.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' This is the broken (irregular) plural of ḥadīqah ('garden'). Its final ending is a plain -a (fatḥa) with NO tanwīn, because this plural pattern is 'diptote' — a class of nouns that refuses the -n (nunation) and uses -a for the accusative. It is the object of 'We caused to grow.'
1.root: ح-د-ق (ḥ-d-q) — to enclose, surround (hence an enclosed garden)

2.meaning: Dense, lush — describing the orchards as thick-growing, with tall trees and abundant foliage.
2.grammar: A plural describing the gardens as 'dense/lush.' Although it describes ḥadāʾiq, it does NOT carry tanwīn through plain adjectival agreement: ḥadāʾiq (id 81) is a diptote and takes -a WITHOUT tanwīn, so an agreeing adjective would likewise be diptote (غُلۡبَ). Instead, غُلۡبًا is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) — 'the gardens, [being] dense' — an indefinite triptote, which is why it legitimately takes the full -an (tanwīn fatḥ) in the accusative.
2.root: غ-ل-ب (gh-l-b) — to be thick, stout, overpowering

1.meaning: And fruit — produce/fruits in general that people enjoy and benefit from.
1.grammar: 'And fruit.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The noun is feminine (its ending ة 'tied tā' is sounded as -t before the case vowel). The final -tan (tanwīn fatḥ on the feminine ending) is the accusative — it continues the list of things made to grow — and marks it as indefinite.

2.meaning: and grass/herbage; specifically lush pasturage and fodder — the dense green growth that grazing animals feed on. It is paired with 'fruit' to evoke the full bounty Allah brings forth from the earth.
2.grammar: A noun joined by 'wa' (and). The conjunction 'wa' is invariable — it simply means 'and'. The final '-an' (written with tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative ending: it marks the word as an object in the list of things caused to grow, and it also signals that the word is indefinite ('some fodder'). Note: in recitation the tanwīn (-an) of the preceding word 'fākihah(tan)' merges into this 'wa' (a Tajweed feature called idghām), which is why the wāw is recited with a doubling — this is a pronunciation rule, not a change to the conjunction itself.
2.root: أ-ب-ب (ʾ-b-b) — fresh pasture, herbage that animals graze

1.meaning: a provision / means of enjoyment and sustenance — something granted for you to benefit from and live on for a while. The word carries the sense of temporary, enjoyable supply that meets a need.
1.grammar: A noun with the accusative '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa). Here the accusative works adverbially, telling us the purpose/manner — 'as a provision' — explaining why all the foregoing was made to grow. The '-an' also marks it as indefinite. Note on the written form: in the muṣḥaf the initial mīm carries a shadda (مَّتَاعًا) because the tanwīn (-an) of the preceding word 'abban' merges into this mīm in recitation (a Tajweed idghām); the base word itself is simply 'matāʿ', and this doubling is a pronunciation feature, not part of the stem.
1.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to provide enjoyment, benefit, or supply

2.meaning: for you (plural) — denoting benefit or possession directed toward a group of people: 'for your sake, for your use.'
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (for/to) fused with the attached pronoun '-kum' = 'you (plural)' → 'for you all'. The phrase shows who benefits: the provision is for you. Note: the preposition keeps its vowel 'li-' before a pronoun (it does not change to 'la-'). In the written/recited form the lām appears doubled because the tanwīn (-an) of the preceding word 'matāʿan' merges into this lām (a Tajweed idghām) — a pronunciation feature, not a change in the preposition's vowel.

3.meaning: and for your livestock — the grazing animals (camels, cattle, sheep, goats) that people own and depend on. It extends the provision beyond humans to the beasts in their care.
3.grammar: 'wa' (and) + the preposition 'li-' (for) + the noun 'anʿām' (livestock) + the attached pronoun '-kum' (your, plural). Because 'li-' governs the noun, 'anʿām' takes the genitive case (its '-i' ending, here followed directly by the pronoun): literally 'and for the-livestock-of you.' 'Anʿām' is itself a plural ('grazing animals collectively').

1.meaning: but/then when — introduces a future scenario and signals that a decisive consequence is about to follow. 'Idhā' points to something certain to happen ('when', not a doubtful 'if'); the prefixed 'fa-' links it to what came before as a result ('so/then, when…').
1.grammar: Two particles joined: 'fa-' (then/so), which connects this to the previous statement as a sequel, plus 'idhā', a time-word meaning 'when' that anticipates a definite future event and sets up its main clause. No case ending applies — these are invariable particles.

2.meaning: it comes / arrives — the act of coming to pass, drawing near and reaching one. Here it conveys the sudden onset of the foretold event.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it came'), agreeing with the feminine noun that follows (aṣ-ṣākhah). The final '-i' is not a case ending but a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word beginning with 'al-'.

3.meaning: the Deafening Blast — a name for the overwhelming Cry of the Day of Resurrection, a sound so piercing it almost bursts the hearing. It denotes the catastrophic shout/trumpet that ushers in the end.
3.grammar: The definite article 'al-' (the) + an intensive noun-form 'ṣākhah' (one that deafens). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following emphatic 'ṣ' (a sun-letter), so it is recited 'aṣ-ṣākhah'. The final '-u' is the nominative ending: it marks this word as the doer/subject of the verb 'came' — it is the Blast that comes.
3.root: ص-خ-خ (ṣ-kh-kh) — to deafen with a piercing sound; to strike the ear violently

1.meaning: the Day — a specific appointed day; here it points to the Day of Resurrection, functioning as 'on the Day that…' to frame what will happen then.
1.grammar: A noun meaning 'day'. The final '-a' ending is accusative, used here adverbially to mean 'on (that) Day' — it pins the following events to a point in time. It governs the verb-clause that follows ('the Day [on which] every person flees…').
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: he flees / will flee — to run away in fright, escaping from someone. The form expresses an ongoing or future fleeing, capturing the panic of that Day.
2.grammar: A present/future verb. The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he…'). The final '-u' is the indicative ending, signalling a plain ongoing or future action ('flees / will flee') with nothing cutting it off. The doubled 'rr' is the root's natural gemination.
2.root: ف-ر-ر (f-r-r) — to flee, run away, escape

3.meaning: the man / the person — here generic, 'every individual,' standing for any human being who will flee on that Day.
3.grammar: The definite article 'al-' (the) + the noun 'marʾ' (man/person). The final '-u' is the nominative ending, marking this as the subject — the one who does the fleeing ('the person flees'). Used generically, it means 'each and every person.'

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'from' — it marks origin, source, or starting point: out of, from, made of. Here it asks about the material origin of a human being.
4.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (it never changes form). It governs the word after it, putting that word into the genitive case. Here it links to 'ayyi shay'in' to ask 'OUT OF what thing…?'

5.meaning: his brother — a male sibling; by extension a close kinsman. Listed among the very people one would normally cling to, yet from whom one flees in terror.
5.grammar: The noun 'akh' (brother) — one of a special group of nouns that show their case with a long vowel — appears here as 'akhī' with a long '-ī', which is its genitive form because it follows the preposition 'min' (from) in the verse ('flees from…'). The attached pronoun '-hi' means 'his'; its vowel is '-hi' (not '-hu') because it follows that '-ī' sound. Altogether: 'from his brother.'

1.meaning: and his mother — the one who bore and nurtured him; named here, alongside the father, as the most tender of bonds that the terror of that Day will override.
1.grammar: 'wa' (and) + the noun 'umm' (mother) + the attached pronoun '-hi' (his). The noun carries a genitive '-i' ending because it continues under the preposition 'min' (from) governing this list ('from… and his mother'). The pronoun is '-hi' (with 'i', and here a long '-hī' in recitation) because it follows that '-i' vowel. The doubled 'mm' is part of the root.

2.meaning: And his father — the male parent. Here it appears in a list of the closest relatives a person will flee from on the Day of Judgment.
2.grammar: A noun ('father') in the genitive case, followed by the attached pronoun 'his.' It is genitive because it is a coordinate member of the earlier prepositional phrase introduced by 'from' (min): 'from his brother, and his mother, and his father…'; the preposition governs the whole coordinated list, not just the word immediately after it. This word belongs to a small set of nouns ('father, brother, father-in-law…') that take a long -ī before a possessive ending instead of a short case-vowel; the genitive therefore shows up as -ī rather than -i. The final 'hi' (rather than 'hu') is simply how 'his' is pronounced after that -ī sound.

1.meaning: And his female companion — i.e. his wife/spouse, the woman who accompanies him through life.
1.grammar: A feminine noun ('companion, consort'), built as the feminine of ṣāḥib ('companion'), in the genitive case (a coordinate member of the preceding 'from' phrase); the -i ending is the genitive marker that also links the noun to the possessor. The attached 'hi' means 'his,' and it is pronounced 'hi' (not 'hu') because it follows the -i vowel.

2.meaning: And his sons/children — his male offspring (commonly rendered 'children'). The list moves from parents to spouse to one's own offspring.
2.grammar: The plural of ibn ('son'), here in the genitive case (a coordinate member of the preceding 'from' phrase). This is a 'sound masculine plural,' whose genitive/accusative form ends in -īn; when a possessive pronoun is attached, the final -n drops, leaving banī- before the suffix. The attached 'hi' means 'his' and is pronounced 'hi' after the -ī. So the form literally reads 'and his sons.'
2.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring, to build

1.meaning: For each one / for every single one — introducing the idea that every individual person, without exception, is meant.
1.grammar: The preposition li- ('for, to') attached to the word kull ('every, each'). Because li- is a preposition, the noun after it must take the genitive case, which is why the ending is -i (kulli). It governs the next word ('every man'), giving 'for every man.'

2.meaning: A man / a single human individual — here used in the general sense of 'every person.'
2.grammar: The noun imruʾ ('man, person'). It is in the genitive case because it follows the word kull ('every') from the previous word, so 'every' and 'man' join as 'every man.' The ending -in is the indefinite genitive (the doubled vowel/tanwīn carrying both 'genitive case' and the sense of 'a/an'). Unusually, this noun also carries a matching case-vowel on its first root letter (the hamza), a feature special to imruʾ; note the final root letter is itself a hamza (ʾ), part of the root م-ر-أ.

3.meaning: From among them — singling out individuals out of a larger group (here, out of all people).
3.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Together they mean 'from among them.' The doubled 'm' at the start (mim-min in recitation) is an assimilation with the previous word's ending and does not change the meaning. The pronoun is fixed in form and does not take a case ending.

4.meaning: On that Day — i.e. the Day of Resurrection. It pins the statement to that specific, decisive Day.
4.grammar: A compound of yawm ('day') plus -idhin ('then, at that moment'), fused into one word meaning 'on that day.' It functions as a time-adverb ('when/on that day'). The -in ending here is a tanwīn that compensates for an implied clause ('the day when [all this happens]'); the whole word is treated as fixed in the accusative, doing the work of 'on that day.'

5.meaning: A concern / an affair that preoccupies — a matter or situation serious enough to absorb a person's whole attention.
5.grammar: The noun shaʾn ('affair, matter, concern'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (the doubled vowel/tanwīn meaning 'a/an' and marking the subject). It is the subject of the sentence: 'each person will have [a concern] that occupies him,' so it stands in the nominative ('a matter… [exists] for him').
5.root: ش-أ-ن (sh-ʾ-n) — affair, matter, state of concern

6.meaning: That keeps him fully occupied / suffices to absorb him — a concern so consuming it leaves him no attention for anyone else.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, 'he/it engrosses, suffices for,' (Form IV of the root) with the attached object pronoun -hi ('him'). The 'yu-' prefix marks 'he/it' as the doer; the verb describes the 'concern' from the previous word, so 'a concern that occupies him.' The verb's own ending is the long -ī (yughnī), the normal ending for this kind of verb whose final root letter is a weak/long vowel. The attached 'hi' ('him') is pronounced 'hi' after that -ī. The doubled 'y' at the start is recitation assimilation with the preceding tanwīn and carries no extra meaning.
6.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — sufficiency, being free of need / engrossment

1.meaning: Faces — i.e. people seen through their faces; here it begins the description of how people will look on Judgment Day.
1.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of wajh ('face'), so it means 'faces.' The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (doubled vowel/tanwīn meaning 'some… ' and marking it as the subject): it is the subject being described — 'faces, on that Day, [will be] bright.'
1.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

2.meaning: On that Day — again the Day of Resurrection, anchoring the description to that moment.
2.grammar: The same compound as before: yawm ('day') + -idhin ('then'), fused to mean 'on that day,' working as a time-adverb. The -in ending is a tanwīn compensating for an implied clause ('the day when…'); the word is fixed in the accusative as 'on that day.' The doubled 'y' at the start is recitation assimilation with the preceding tanwīn (wujūhun → wujūhuy-yawma) and adds no meaning.

3.meaning: Bright and beaming — shining with light, radiant with joy and good news.
3.grammar: An active participle (Form IV of the root meaning 'to shine, gleam'), in its feminine form to agree with 'faces,' so 'shining, radiant.' The base form of the word is مُسْفِرَة (musfira), with a single mīm. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative (doubled vowel/tanwīn): it describes the subject 'faces,' hence 'faces… [will be] bright.' In recitation the preceding word's tanwīn assimilates into this mīm (yawmaʾidhin + musfiratun → yawmaʾidhim-musfiratun), which is why a doubling can be heard at the start; that doubling is a phonetic feature of the recitation, not part of the word itself.

1.meaning: An active participle (feminine singular) describing faces that are 'laughing'—radiant, smiling, lit up with joy. It depicts the joyful state of the believers on the Day of Resurrection.
1.grammar: An active participle on the pattern fāʿil ('one who does X'), made feminine by the -at ending to agree with 'faces' (wujūh). The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, because it is a predicate describing the subject 'faces': 'faces that are laughing.'

2.meaning: An active participle (feminine singular) meaning 'rejoicing at good news'—beaming with delight at glad tidings. The Form X (istafʿala) verb adds the sense of actively seeking or receiving joyful news, so the faces glow with happy anticipation of reward.
2.grammar: An active participle of a Form X (istafʿala) verb, giving the pattern mustafʿil: the prefix mu- forms the participle ('one who...'), and sta- is the Form X stem marker (the participle drops the initial alif of ista-, but keeps the sīn and tā). The tā here belongs to that Form X sta- prefix, not to any infix. Form X often adds the sense of seeking or receiving. The -at makes it feminine to agree with 'faces,' and the -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative as a second predicate: '(faces that are) rejoicing at good news.'

1.meaning: 'And faces'—the conjunction 'and' joined to the plural noun 'faces.' This introduces the contrasting group: in opposition to the joyful faces, there will be other faces in misery.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and.' Wujūh is the broken (irregular) plural of wajh ('face'). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative, as the subject of a new clause being described: 'and (other) faces...'

2.meaning: On that Day — again the Day of Resurrection, anchoring the description to that moment.
2.grammar: The same compound as before: yawm ('day') + -idhin ('then'), fused to mean 'on that day,' working as a time-adverb. The -in ending is a tanwīn compensating for an implied clause ('the day when…'); the word is fixed in the accusative as 'on that day.' The doubled 'y' at the start is recitation assimilation with the preceding tanwīn (wujūhun → wujūhuy-yawma) and adds no meaning.

3.meaning: 'Upon them' / 'on them'—the preposition 'on/upon' with an attached feminine plural pronoun referring back to the faces. It sets up what lies over those faces.
3.grammar: ʿalā ('on/upon') takes its connecting form ʿalay- before a suffix. The attached pronoun -hā means 'her/them' and here refers to the (grammatically feminine) 'faces.' Together they form a phrase placed first for emphasis: 'upon them (will be)...'

4.meaning: 'Dust' / 'dustiness'—a layer of grime or dust settling on the faces, a mark of grief, humiliation, and distress on that Day.
4.grammar: A noun naming a state or condition (dust covering something). The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative, because it is the delayed subject of the clause 'upon them (will be) dust.'

1.meaning: 'It covers them' / 'will overcome them'—a present-tense verb meaning to overspread, envelop, or overwhelm. The darkness rises up and engulfs those faces.
1.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb. The ta- prefix marks a 3rd-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'), agreeing with the feminine subject 'darkness' (qatarah) that follows. The -u ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact). The attached -hā ('them') is the object, referring to the faces: 'darkness covers them.'
1.root: ر-ه-ق (r-h-q) — to cover over, overwhelm, oppress

2.meaning: 'Darkness' / 'blackness'—a dark gloom or soot-like shroud, the blackening of the faces in shame and despair, layered over the dust mentioned before.
2.grammar: A noun denoting darkness or a smoky black covering. The final -un (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and nominative, as the subject of the verb that precedes it: '(there) covers them darkness.'

1.meaning: 'Those' / 'those ones'—a far-pointing demonstrative ('those over there') used for people. It gathers up the people just described and points to them: 'those (very people) are...'
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those.' The -ka element signals distance ('over there'). It is indeclinable (its ending never changes for case) and here serves as the subject: 'those are...' The long marks reflect the lengthened, emphatic pronunciation of this fixed word.

2.meaning: An emphasizing pronoun 'they'—placed between 'those' and 'the disbelievers' to stress identity: 'those, they are the very ones who...' It underlines that precisely these people, and no others, are meant.
2.grammar: The detached pronoun 'they' (masculine plural). Its base form is hum; the final vowel is read -u (humu) to ease pronunciation before the following 'al-.' Here it works as a pronoun of separation/emphasis, reinforcing that 'those' are identical to 'the disbelievers.'

3.meaning: 'The disbelievers'—those who reject faith. This particular plural (kafarah) carries an intensive, blunt force, naming them flatly as the ingrate deniers of the truth.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- ('the') plus the plural kafarah on the intensive pattern faʿalah (used for groups marked by a trait). The final -u marks the nominative case, as the predicate identifying 'those': 'those... are the disbelievers.' Being definite (with al-), it takes a plain -u with no tanwīn.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'The wicked' / 'the depraved sinners'—those who brazenly break the bounds of right, the immoral evildoers. It is a second, intensifying description piled onto 'the disbelievers.'
4.grammar: A definite plural noun: al- ('the') plus the plural fajarah on the intensive pattern faʿalah ('those marked by debauchery'). The final -u marks the nominative case, as a further predicate describing the same people: '...the disbelievers, the wicked.' Being definite (with al-), it takes a plain -u with no tanwīn.
4.root: ف-ج-ر (f-j-r) — to break out into sin, debauchery, wickedness
